capabilities.title: Text embossing and font loading
capabilities.cost: part built: `crates/font` reads TrueType outlines and measured against FreeType, `crates/text` extrudes them into a closed prism, `hfw-cli --text` slices one, and `hfw_text_mesh` hands the same prism to the application as a mesh handle to add as a part or a negative volume. Left: kerning and shaping (advances are plain `hmtx` widths), placing text on an object's surface, and CFF-flavoured fonts
capabilities.note: `docs/TEXT.md` is the design note and the measured state.

capabilities.title: Cut, hollow and split
capabilities.cost: part built: `Mesh::cut` splits a closed mesh by a plane and caps both halves, capping holes as well, and `Mesh::parts` splits separate shells; both cross the ABI as `hfw_mesh_cut` and `hfw_mesh_part` and are measured by volume and by closed-surface diagnostics. Left: hollowing, an inward shell with a wall thickness and drain holes, which needs a mesh offset the engine does not have — the 2D offsets it does have work per layer, so a hollowed body still has to arrive hollowed
capabilities.note: A cut body arrives as two closed meshes; a hollowed one still has to arrive hollowed.

capabilities.title: Nesting arranger
capabilities.cost: interlocking 2D packing with rotations and a search; the shelf packer here fills rows and turns a part a quarter turn, so a bed whose parts only fit interlocked is refused
capabilities.note: `hfw_plate_arrange` is the shelf packer, and it stays as the fast path.

capabilities.title: AMF reading
capabilities.cost: an XML model with vertices, triangles and materials — small next to the 3MF reader already here
capabilities.note: STL, 3MF and OBJ are read; AMF is not.

capabilities.title: Internal bridges
capabilities.cost: detect a bridge whose support is infill rather than air, and give it the bridging flow and direction; the external bridge path exists

capabilities.title: Tiled distance field
capabilities.cost: tile the per-layer mask so a 200 mm plate at 0.05 mm stops being refused for memory (~450 MB today)
capabilities.note: A large thin plate at a fine layer height is refused rather than slowed.

capabilities.title: Vendor G-code placeholders
capabilities.cost: substitute the dialect's whole placeholder set (`[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]`, `{during_print_exhaust_fan_speed_num[current_extruder]}` and the rest) in start and end G-code
capabilities.note: A real vendor machine preset leaves them literal today and the verifier rejects the file.

capabilities.title: Slicing mode and hole closing
capabilities.cost: done: `slicing_mode` is regular, even_odd (the rule slice assembly already
capabilities.note: uses) or close_holes, which fills the void in every layer.

capabilities.title: STEP and IGES import
capabilities.cost: B-rep tessellation needs an OCCT-class kernel, which is the one dependency this project has refused so far
capabilities.blocked_on: the dependency decision: a C++ CAD kernel in the build
capabilities.note: Nothing here reads a parametric solid.

capabilities.title: A gated corpus against libslic3r
capabilities.cost: drive libslic3r through its own API on a fixed corpus and diff the toolpaths, rather than comparing exported G-code on six fixtures
capabilities.note: `scripts/oracle.py` is the fixture-level version of this.

capabilities.title: Tool paint: a facet's extruder
capabilities.cost: a third paint channel, consumed by stack assignment
capabilities.note: `Paint` carries support and seam only: a channel nothing reads is a control that does nothing.

capabilities.title: Multi-material: MMU, AMS, wipe tower
capabilities.cost: per-facet tool assignment, strand ordering, purge and a wipe tower, and the 56 settings in `docs/SETTINGS-GAPS.md`'s multi-material bucket
capabilities.blocked_on: the owner has no tool changer or MMU yet

capabilities.title: Resin (SLA/MSLA) slicing
capabilities.cost: a second pipeline: exposure masks per layer, resin supports, and a writer that commands light instead of extrusion
capabilities.blocked_on: the owner has ruled it out — a different process, not a gap
capabilities.note: Ruled out by the owner: the pipeline here is filament.

settings.name: avoid_crossing_perimeters
settings.hfw: avoid_crossing_perimeters — on by default, and it does two things: the emitter orders a layer's paths by nearest entry, and it routes the travel itself around the loops — each loop offset both ways by a bead of clearance, a visibility graph over those offset rings, and the route emitted as one retracted chain of moves. A closed loop keeps the seam the profile chose unless the seam is `nearest`, so routing costs distance and never the seam. Measured on `fixtures/stress_gear.stl`: 777 travels cross a printed perimeter with the switch off, 757 with it on, so 2.6% of the crossings this part produces are what routing and ordering can remove. What is left is not a bug in the router: a travel that begins inside a closed loop cannot leave it without crossing the loop, and two islands printed one after the other need a route between them that does not exist at that layer. Upstream reduces those by planning the layer as a whole, which this engine does not do yet

settings.name: avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour
settings.hfw: avoid_crossing_perimeters_max_detour — caps both the entry-point choice and the routed travel: a route longer than the straight move plus this budget is refused and the straight move is emitted instead. Zero means no limit, so the shipped profiles route without a ceiling

settings.name: bed_custom_model
settings.hfw: bed_custom_model — the mesh is sliced halfway up its height and its largest ring becomes `bed_shape`, so packing uses the outline's box, centring moves a part into the outline and one that does not sit inside it is refused with the vertex count rather than a printed point list. Holes in a bed mesh are not holes in the printable area: `bed_shape` is one polygon, which is the same limit a hand-written outline has

settings.name: bed_custom_texture
settings.hfw: bed_custom_texture — recorded in the profile and echoed to the panel, which is the only thing that draws a bed; the engine has no viewport and no surface a texture could change

settings.name: binary_gcode
settings.hfw: binary_gcode — a profile that sets it writes the bgcode container instead of the text file: the same G-code in a gcode block, the thumbnails in blocks of their own, metadata in INI blocks and every block CRC32-checksummed. Nothing is compressed and nothing is MeatPack-encoded, because the specification allows both values to be 0 and this writer only emits those; a machine that insists on a compressed block is not served yet, which is a size optimisation rather than a second format. The C ABI still returns the text (`hfw_gcode_text`), so today the container is the command line's

settings.name: elefant_foot_compensation
settings.hfw: elefant_foot_compensation — shrinks the first layer's cross-section by the value, on the printed outline, so walls, infill, skin and the brim all follow the compensated layer. The offset is taken on the whole region at once, so a hole smaller than twice the value closes instead of turning inside out. Where the offset merges or opens a feature is decided on a grid of one third of the value (0.02 mm floor), and every vertex is then walked onto the exact offset from the contour it came from

settings.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_positive
settings.hfw: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_positive — solved per bead path against the widest section on it, so a widening bead cannot push its own rate past the cap and a narrowing one pays its wide end's price. What is not done is what upstream does: splitting the move, so that two beads of different width meeting at a path boundary cannot step the rate between them. Measured on taper_wall, that boundary step reaches 6.2 mm3/s2 against a 4 mm3/s2 cap

settings.name: slice_closing_radius
settings.hfw: slice_closing_radius — fills cracks narrower than twice the value and drops holes smaller than it, on the sliced cross-section before compensation or simplification. Implemented by pulling the two boundary pieces together onto their midpoint rather than by an offset and back in, so a layer without a crack is left bit-identical instead of carrying a grid's error; the cost is that a concave corner is not rounded by the radius the way upstream's closing rounds it

settings.name: slicing_mode
settings.hfw: slicing_mode — `close_holes` fills every void in a layer: the ring set is reduced to the boundaries no other ring contains, so a hole prints over and an island that sat inside one becomes part of the same solid. `even_odd` is the same output as `regular`, and deliberately so: slice assembly already treats a stack of contours by the even-odd rule, so there is no second path to take. Measured on `fixtures/torus.stl`, close_holes prints 914.8 mm of filament against 831.5 mm, and the verifier passes both

settings.name: support_material_synchronize_layers
settings.hfw: support_material_synchronize_layers — the boundaries always coincide: this engine plans one layer schedule for the whole job, support included, so a support layer begins and ends where the object's layer does. The reference only needs the option because a multi-extruder preset can print support at a coarser height than the part it holds up, and this engine has no second schedule to coarsen. The flag is recorded so a profile that asks for it round trips unchanged

settings.name: top_fill_pattern
settings.hfw: top_fill_pattern — all eight patterns are drawn: the five straight and concentric ones from this engine's own fill, and hilbertcurve, archimedeanchords and octagramspiral from upstream's plane-path curves clipped to the skin mask. monotonic and monotoniclines share one geometry because this engine's emitter decides the joining, not the fill

settings.name: top_infill_extrusion_width

settings.name: wall_distribution_count
settings.hfw: wall_distribution_count — spreads the difference between the outer loop's width and the inner ones over the band with upstream's parabolic weights, centred on the middle loop. This engine's beading already places each bead from the geometry through the medial axis, so the only difference it has to distribute is that outer-width one; one loop is the default and reproduces the undistributed band exactly
